headline: A developer planning a data centre on a park-and-ride site in Cardiff has asked for permission to build a temporary gas power plant to run it.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a named UK project with wide political objection, but a single local case reported by one outlet.
importance_line: Residents near the Llanrumney site worry about noise, fumes and the nearby hospital, and the case feeds a wider Welsh debate over national data centre policy, though the developer says the gas plant is only a worst case and may use fuel cells instead.
summary: BBC News reports that the developer Curtis Hall is seeking permission for a temporary gas power plant of up to 49.9 megawatts, running for up to five years from July 2028, to power its proposed Cardiff data centre if the site cannot get a grid connection in time, which it calls a 'worst-case scenario'. Friends of the Earth Cymru calls the plan 'climate-wrecking', almost all the area's Members of the Senedd (the Welsh parliament) and a Welsh government minister have objected, and the Welsh government is considering taking over the planning decision and plans its own data centre policy by the end of the year.
notes: Read in full. The BBC does not say when the gas plan was first disclosed; objections were lodged this week.
